S1.concept: Data has value only through the decision it informs. Knowing where your data comes from is the first step to questioning it.

spark.hook: One exception log, three different answers. Which source would you trust, and why?

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Why data matters to a decision; data types and where they come from.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Map the sources you use in your own role, and how each reaches you.

S1.build: Map every data source used in your role: origin, owner, refresh cadence, format, and the decision each one feeds.
howTo: List the decisions you make or support each week.
Name the data behind each decision and where it comes from.
Record owner, format and refresh cadence for each source.
Flag any source you use but could not explain.
reflect: Which decision in your role rests on data you have never questioned?
Where did you assume data was someone else's job?
One source you will trace back to its origin this week.

S2.concept: Bad data rarely announces itself. Completeness and consistency checks catch it before it quietly shapes a decision.

spark.hook: A QC sample looked clean until someone counted the blanks.

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Common quality failures: missing values, inconsistent codes, duplicates, stale records.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Build a quality checklist and test it on a mock dataset from your function.

S2.build: Build a data quality checklist for a dataset you use, then test it on a safe mock version.
howTo: Choose one dataset you rely on in your function.
Write checks for completeness, consistency, duplicates and timeliness.
Run each check on the mock version and log failures.
Note how each failure could reach a decision unnoticed.
reflect: Which quality failure would most likely slip past you today?
What would you now question before trusting a figure?
One check you will run before your next report.

S3.concept: Governance tells you what may be shared, uploaded or combined. Handling rules come before analysis, not after it.

spark.hook: Can this risk extract go into Copilot Chat? Decide before you paste.

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Governance basics, data classification, and the readiness diagnostic.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Write handling rules for the data you touch, including AI-assistance limits.

S3.build: Complete the readiness diagnostic, then write a data handling checklist for the data your role touches.
howTo: Complete the readiness diagnostic individually.
List the data types you handle and their classification.
For each, note what may be shared, uploaded or combined.
Mark anything needing anonymisation or mock data before AI use.
reflect: Which data do you handle that must never go into AI assistance?
How does governance change what you treat as usable evidence?
Complete the mindset pulse before you leave.

S4.concept: Messy data is normal. A repeatable cleaning routine turns it into something you can analyse yourself, without raising a request.

spark.hook: Same broker, four spellings, two date formats. Can you trust the pipeline count?

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Spotting mess: blanks, mixed formats, duplicates, inconsistent labels.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Clean a mock dataset from your own function and log each step.

S4.build: Clean a messy mock dataset from your function in Excel, using AI assistance to suggest steps, and log every change.
howTo: Profile the dataset: blanks, formats, duplicates, odd values.
Ask AI assistance to suggest cleaning steps for the issues found.
Apply each step in Excel and record what changed.
Compare row counts and totals before and after cleaning.
reflect: Which cleaning step would you previously have sent to an analyst?
How do you know your cleaning did not remove valid records?
One messy file you will clean yourself this month.

S5.concept: Shape data once, then repeat it. A documented transformation routine makes next month's preparation faster and consistent.

spark.hook: Month-end reconciliation rebuilt by hand every month. What if the steps were saved?

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Shaping data for analysis: columns, types, layout, derived fields.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Build and document transformation steps you can rerun next month.

S5.build: Turn a mock monthly extract from your function into a reusable preparation routine, documented so a colleague could rerun it.
howTo: Decide the shape your analysis needs: rows, columns, types.
Build each transformation step in Excel or the preparation tool.
Document the steps in order, in plain language.
Rerun the routine on a second month's mock extract.
reflect: Which monthly task do you rebuild from scratch each time?
What would a colleague need to rerun your routine without you?
One preparation routine you will document this week.

S6.concept: Combining sources adds value only if the join holds. Always check row counts and unmatched records after joining.

spark.hook: The joined list had more rows than either source. What went wrong?

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Join types, keys, and how joins break: duplicates, mismatched formats.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Combine two mock datasets from your function and prove the join held.

S6.build: Combine two mock datasets from your function using a lookup or merge, then verify the result with counts and unmatched checks.
howTo: Identify a shared key and check it is unique.
Standardise key formats in both datasets before joining.
Join with a lookup or merge in Excel or the preparation tool.
Reconcile row counts and list unmatched records.
reflect: How would you have spotted a broken join before this session?
Which combined dataset in your work has never been checked?
One check you will always run after a join.

S7.concept: Formulas and lookups answer business questions directly. The skill is choosing the right calculation and checking it.

spark.hook: Variance commentary waits days for figures. Could a lookup answer it today?

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Core formulas and lookups applied to real business questions.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Complete two analyses on a mock dataset from your function.

S7.build: Answer two business questions from your function using formulas and lookups on a permitted or mock dataset.
howTo: Write each business question in one sentence.
Choose the formulas and lookups the question needs.
Use AI assistance to explain or debug a formula, not to decide.
Check results against a manual total or known figure.
reflect: Which question could you now answer without raising a request?
How did you check the formula gave the right answer?
One routine question you will answer yourself next week.

S8.concept: Pivots summarise thousands of rows in seconds. The judgement is in how you group, and what the summary hides.

spark.hook: Vendor spend by category looked fine until it was grouped by month.

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Pivots, grouping and summarising at scale.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Build a summarised view of a permitted or mock dataset from your function.

S8.build: Summarise a permitted or mock dataset from your function with pivots, then test whether a different grouping changes the story.
howTo: Decide what the summary must answer before building it.
Build a pivot with the grouping that fits the question.
Regroup by another field and compare the picture.
Reconcile pivot totals to the source data.
reflect: What did a different grouping reveal that the first one hid?
Which summary in your work might be hiding something?
One summary you will rebuild and recheck yourself.

S9.concept: A sharp question picks the right measure. Test whether the answer holds before anyone acts on it.

spark.hook: Complaints are up. Per what, compared with when, and does it matter?

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Turning a vague request into a precise question with the right measure.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Answer one framed question from your function and document the method.

S9.build: Frame a business question from your function, choose its measure, answer it, and document the method and its limits.
howTo: Rewrite a vague request as one precise question.
Choose the measure and comparison that answers it.
Answer it, then test with another period or segment.
Document method, assumptions and limits in a few lines.
reflect: How did reframing the question change the answer?
Would your answer hold if someone tested it differently?
One request you will reframe before starting analysis.

S10.concept: The right chart answers the question at a glance. Remove everything the reader does not need.

spark.hook: Twelve colours, three axes, no conclusion. What is this chart asking?

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Matching chart type to question; decluttering and labelling.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Build three charts that each answer one question from your function.

S10.build: Build three charts from an aggregated, anonymised dataset in your function, each answering one stated question.
howTo: Write the question each chart must answer.
Pick the chart type that best fits each question.
Remove gridlines, legends and colours the reader does not need.
Title each chart with its answer, not its topic.
reflect: Could a reader get your answer without you explaining it?
What did you remove, and did the chart get clearer?
One chart in your regular reporting you will simplify.

S11.concept: A dashboard works only if a decision-maker can read it alone. Design for the decision, not the data.

spark.hook: The shift lead opened the dashboard and asked, 'So what do I do?'

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Dashboard layout: decision first, key measures, minimal clutter.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Build a working dashboard for a decision in your function.

S11.build: Build a working dashboard in Excel or the dashboard tool (to be confirmed) for one decision in your function.
howTo: Name the decision and the person who makes it.
Choose three to five measures that inform that decision.
Lay out the most important measure first, top left.
Test it with a peer who has no explanation.
reflect: Could your peer act on the dashboard without asking you?
Which report request could this dashboard replace?
One change to make the dashboard readable alone.

S12.concept: Numbers do not speak for themselves. A short narrative connects the finding to the decision it should change.

spark.hook: Session feedback scores rose. So what should the team do next?

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Structuring an insight: finding, evidence, implication, recommendation.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Write and present an insight summary from your function to a non-technical peer.

S12.build: Write an insight summary and narrative for an analysis from your function, then present it to a non-technical peer.
howTo: State the finding in one sentence a non-specialist understands.
Add two pieces of supporting evidence and one caveat.
Use AI assistance to tighten wording; check every figure yourself.
Present in three minutes and note listener questions.
reflect: Which question from your listener exposed a gap in your story?
Did AI assistance change any meaning you had to correct?
One insight you will present yourself rather than send as a table.

S13.concept: Review catches what the author misses. Correcting each other's analysis builds the habit of checking before relying.

spark.hook: An audit sample reviewer found the total right but the method wrong.

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Review method: question, data, method, result, visual.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Peer-review a colleague's analysis and visuals, then improve your own.

S13.build: Swap an analysis and its visuals with a peer, review against a shared checklist, then correct your own work.
howTo: Agree a review checklist covering data, method, result and visual.
Review your peer's work and note specific issues.
Discuss findings and agree what to change.
Correct your own analysis and record what changed.
reflect: What did your reviewer catch that you had missed?
How will you check your own work before sharing next time?
One habit from peer review you will keep.

S14.concept: The best opportunities hide in routine work. Find where a data-driven view could change a decision, then size it.

spark.hook: Onboarding status is tracked in three places. Who sees the whole picture?

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Spotting data-driven opportunities in your own recurring work.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Identify and size three candidate opportunities from your function.

S14.build: Identify at least three data-driven opportunities in your own work and size the value of each.
howTo: List recurring reports, requests and decisions in your role.
Mark where data arrives late, scattered or unchecked.
Describe three opportunities as a decision plus a better view.
Size each by time, frequency and decision affected.
reflect: Which routine report could become a view your team uses?
What would change if that decision had better data?
One opportunity you would put to your manager.

S15.concept: Your manager validates business value. Prepare a short, evidenced conversation and select one opportunity together.

spark.hook: Two strong ideas, one manager. Which one solves a problem they recognise?

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Preparing the manager conversation: problem, value, data, effort.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Prepare your case, run the manager conversation, and select one opportunity.

S15.build: Prepare a one-page summary of your three opportunities, run the manager conversation, and record the selected opportunity.
howTo: Summarise each opportunity: problem, decision, data, effort.
Anticipate your manager's questions and prepare answers.
Run the conversation and listen for their priorities.
Record the selected opportunity and agreed success measure.
reflect: How did your manager's view change the opportunity?
Which team decision will your work actually change?
One thing you will confirm with your manager next.

S16.concept: Permission comes before analysis. Source permitted workplace data, or build safe mock data, for your selected problem.

spark.hook: The real file holds customer details. What does a safe mock version need?

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Locating permitted data; rules for anonymisation and mock data.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Source your working dataset and record its permissions.

S16.build: Locate permitted workplace data for your selected problem, or build safe mock data, and record its permissions.
howTo: List the fields your analysis actually needs.
Confirm with the data owner what you may use.
Remove or mask identifiers, or build a mock equivalent.
Record source, permissions and any handling limits.
reflect: Does your dataset contain only what the decision needs?
Who must agree before your team relies on this data?
One permission you still need to confirm.

S17.concept: Analysis-ready means clean, structured and documented. Apply your earlier routines to the real problem with mentor input.

spark.hook: The application data was clean enough for practice. Is it ready for decisions?

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Applying cleaning and structuring routines to your working dataset.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Prepare your working dataset to analysis-ready with mentor review.

S17.build: Clean and structure your working dataset into an analysis-ready state, documenting each step for mentor review.
howTo: Profile your working dataset for quality issues.
Apply cleaning and transformation steps from your routine.
Document each step so it can be rerun.
Review readiness with your mentor and fix gaps.
reflect: Could your team rerun this preparation without you?
What would make this dataset trustworthy enough to use weekly?
One preparation step you will automate in your routine.

S18.concept: An answer is only useful once checked. Test your analysis before anyone relies on it.

spark.hook: The analysis said error rates fell. Then someone checked the sample size.

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Answering the selected question with the right measures.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Check the answer: reconcile totals, test alternatives, note limits.

S18.build: Answer your selected business question and check the analysis before relying on it.
howTo: Restate the question and the measure agreed with your manager.
Build the analysis on your analysis-ready dataset.
Reconcile totals and test with another period or segment.
Record limits and what would change the answer.
reflect: How confident are you, and what is that confidence based on?
What would your team need to trust this answer weekly?
One check you will repeat each time the data refreshes.

S19.concept: A dashboard earns its place when a decision-maker uses it week to week. Build for that routine.

spark.hook: The insight report arrives monthly. The decisions happen weekly.

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Designing for the weekly decision and its decision-maker.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Build and test the dashboard or report with its intended user.

S19.build: Turn your checked analysis into a working dashboard or report your decision-maker can use week to week.
howTo: Confirm who uses it, when, and for which decision.
Build it in Excel or the dashboard tool (to be confirmed).
Add refresh steps and a short data note.
Test with the intended user and capture their feedback.
reflect: Does your view replace a report, or add another one?
What would stop your team using this every week?
One change your user asked for that you will make.

S20.concept: Impact is estimated honestly, not promised. A one-page plan shows how the team adopts the new view.

spark.hook: The vendor review took weeks. How would you show the difference now?

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Estimating decision or business impact, with stated assumptions.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Write the one-page enablement plan for your team.

S20.build: Estimate the business or decision impact of your work, and write a one-page enablement plan for your team.
howTo: Compare the old and new way: time, steps, handoffs.
State the impact estimate with every assumption visible.
Plan who uses the view, how often, and who maintains it.
Fit it on one page and review with your mentor.
reflect: Which assumption in your estimate is weakest, and how will you test it?
Who in your team needs to change their routine for this to land?
One step to get the view adopted, not just built.

S21.concept: Every useful dataset carries a risk. Name a privacy or governance risk and define a practical mitigation.

spark.hook: The dashboard was useful. It also showed more than its audience should see.

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Identifying privacy and governance risks in your own case.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Define a practical mitigation and record it in your case.

S21.build: Name one data privacy or governance risk in your work and define a practical, owned mitigation.
howTo: Review your data, outputs and audience for exposure risks.
Name the most material risk in one sentence.
Define a mitigation with an owner and a check.
Confirm the analysis informs, never automates, any decision.
reflect: Would your view still be safe if shared one level wider?
How has your idea of usable data changed since Session 3?
Complete the mindset pulse before you leave.

S22.concept: A case persuades when its parts connect: question, analysis, impact, plan and risk tell one story.

spark.hook: Strong reconciliation analysis, scattered across five files. Where is the case?

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Structuring the case: question, analysis, impact, plan, risk.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Assemble your evidence into one complete workplace data case.

S22.build: Pull your analysis, impact estimate, enablement plan and named risk into one complete workplace data case.
howTo: Outline the case from question to recommended decision.
Insert your analysis, impact, plan and risk in order.
Check every figure traces back to the dataset.
Cut anything that does not support the decision.
reflect: Could someone act on your case without you in the room?
Which part of your case is weakest, and why?
One piece of evidence you will strengthen before review.

S23.concept: Review is where a case becomes defensible. Close gaps and tighten evidence before others rely on it.

spark.hook: The reviewer asked one question: 'How do you know?' The case had no answer.

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Mentor review of the full case against agreed criteria.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Close gaps, tighten evidence and correct the case.

S23.build: Take mentor review of your full case, then close gaps, tighten evidence and record each correction.
howTo: Present your case to your mentor in brief.
Log every gap or challenge raised.
Fix evidence, method or narrative for each one.
Recheck figures and confirm the case still holds.
reflect: Which challenge surprised you most, and what did it reveal?
Is this a decision others could act on, or still your numbers?
One correction that made your case more defensible.

S24.concept: Defending a case means anticipating the hard questions. Rehearse the five-minute presentation until the reasoning holds under challenge.

spark.hook: Five minutes, three panel questions. Which one would you dread most?

segments.label: Segment 1
segments.focus: Shaping the five-minute presentation around the decision.

segments.label: Segment 2
segments.focus: Rehearse with challenge questions and refine answers.

S24.build: Rehearse your five-minute presentation and practise answering likely panel questions, if the panel review is approved.
howTo: Cut the case to a five-minute storyline.
Rehearse once, timed, with a peer or mentor.
List the hardest likely questions and draft answers.
Rehearse again and tighten weak answers.
reflect: Which question would test your reasoning, not just your numbers?
Who will act on your decision, and what will you share with them?
Complete the mindset pulse to close the programme.

SELF.concept: Consolidate Stage 1 with curated reading and short videos on data fundamentals and decision-making.

segments.label: Self-paced
segments.focus: Curated reading and videos on data fundamentals and decision-making.

howTo: Work through the curated reading and short videos.
Note one idea each on sources, quality and governance.
Link each idea to a decision in your role.
Bring your consolidated notes to Session 4.
reflect: Which idea most changed how you view your data?
What question will you bring into Stage 2?

CLINIC.concept: Clear blockers from your own data before the applied stage, working them through live with the trainer.

segments.label: Single block
segments.focus: Live blocker clearance on learners' own data problems.

CLINIC.build: Bring one blocker from your own data and work it through with the trainer and peers.
howTo: Write your blocker in one sentence before the clinic.
Share a safe mock or anonymised sample of the problem.
Work it through with the trainer and note the fix.
Record anything still open for Stage 3.
reflect: Which blocker could you now solve yourself next time?
What do you still rely on others to do with data?
Complete the mindset pulse before you leave.

INDEP.concept: Work your analysis between sessions and produce progress artefacts that show the case taking shape.

segments.label: Independent
segments.focus: Analysis work between sessions and progress artefacts.

howTo: Plan independent hours around your Stage 3 milestones.
Work on permitted or mock data only.
Save a dated progress artefact after each work block.
Bring questions and artefacts to your next mentor session.
reflect: What did you complete without needing to ask anyone?
Is your view becoming something your team would use?

useCases.title: Tracing the sources behind exception reporting
useCases.scenario: Exception counts differ between the log, the handover note and the weekly summary. Which source feeds which decision?
useCases.input: Mock servicing exception log, shift handover notes and weekly summary, anonymised.
useCases.aiDoes: A source map showing origin, owner, refresh and the decision each source feeds, with AI assistance drafting the summary.
howTo: List every place exception counts appear.
Trace each count back to its originating source.
Ask AI assistance to tabulate owner, refresh and use.
Mark where counts diverge and why.
useCases.humanCheck: Learner confirms each source and owner with the process, not AI output.
useCases.measure: Number of sources mapped; number of unexplained discrepancies.
useCases.boundary: Mock or anonymised logs only; no account or customer identifiers pasted into AI assistance.

useCases.title: Finding hidden failures in a QC sample
useCases.scenario: A quality-check sample passed review, yet fields were blank, codes inconsistent and some cases duplicated.
useCases.input: Mock QC sample with deliberate blanks, inconsistent outcome codes and duplicate case references.
useCases.aiDoes: A completeness and consistency check in Excel, plus an AI-assisted draft quality checklist.
howTo: Count blanks per field with simple formulas.
List distinct outcome codes and spot inconsistencies.
Flag duplicate case references.
Ask AI assistance to draft a checklist from the failures.
useCases.humanCheck: Learner checks each flagged failure against the sample before adding it to the checklist.
useCases.measure: Number of quality failures found; minutes to run the checklist.
useCases.boundary: Mock sample only; QC outcomes inform review, never individual performance decisions.

useCases.title: Deciding what may go into AI assistance
useCases.scenario: A colleague wants to paste a risk register extract into Copilot Chat. What may be shared, and how?
useCases.input: Mock risk register extract with fields classified by sensitivity.
useCases.aiDoes: A classification of each field as share, mask or exclude, and an AI-assisted handling checklist.
howTo: Classify each field by sensitivity.
Decide share, mask or exclude for each.
Build a safe extract with masked fields.
Ask AI assistance to draft handling rules from decisions.
useCases.humanCheck: Learner confirms classifications against OSBI governance guidance, not AI suggestions.
useCases.measure: Number of fields correctly classified; minutes to produce a safe extract.
useCases.boundary: Copilot Chat via paste or upload only; follow OSBI data classification rules.

useCases.title: Cleaning a messy application pipeline extract
useCases.scenario: A pipeline extract has broker names spelled several ways and mixed date formats, so counts disagree.
useCases.input: Mock mortgage application pipeline extract with inconsistent broker names, date formats and blanks.
useCases.aiDoes: A cleaned dataset with standardised names and dates, and a step log; AI assistance suggests cleaning steps.
howTo: Profile blanks, formats and name variants.
Ask AI assistance to suggest standardisation steps.
Apply steps in Excel and log each change.
Compare counts and totals before and after.
useCases.humanCheck: Learner verifies that no valid applications were merged or dropped.
useCases.measure: Minutes from raw extract to clean dataset; records changed.
useCases.boundary: Mock data only; the dataset informs pipeline reporting, never credit decisions.

useCases.title: A month-end reconciliation routine you can rerun
useCases.scenario: Each month the reconciliation extract is reshaped by hand. Saving the steps would make it repeatable.
useCases.input: Two months of mock ledger and bank-side extracts, anonymised.
useCases.aiDoes: A documented transformation routine in Excel or the preparation tool, with AI assistance explaining steps.
howTo: Define the shape the reconciliation needs.
Build transformation steps on month one.
Document steps in plain language with AI assistance.
Rerun on month two and compare.
useCases.humanCheck: Learner reconciles routine output to control totals for both months.
useCases.measure: Minutes to prepare each month's reconciliation; manual steps remaining.
useCases.boundary: Mock extracts only; no account numbers or real balances in AI assistance.

useCases.title: Joining maturities to contact preferences
useCases.scenario: A maturity list must be joined to contact preferences before outreach. Did the join hold?
useCases.input: Mock savings maturity list and mock contact-preference list sharing a pseudonymised reference.
useCases.aiDoes: A combined dataset with row-count reconciliation and an unmatched-records list; AI assistance explains the lookup.
howTo: Check the reference is unique in both lists.
Standardise reference formats before joining.
Join with a lookup and count matches.
List unmatched and duplicated records.
useCases.humanCheck: Learner reconciles row counts and reviews every unmatched record.
useCases.measure: Rows matched, unmatched and duplicated after the join.
useCases.boundary: Pseudonymised mock data only; no names, contact details or account numbers.

useCases.title: Answering a variance question with lookups
useCases.scenario: A manager asks why a cost line moved against budget. The figures sit in two tables.
useCases.input: Mock budget and actuals tables by cost centre and month.
useCases.aiDoes: Variance by cost centre using formulas and lookups, with AI assistance explaining the formulas.
howTo: State the variance question in one sentence.
Look up budget against actuals by cost centre.
Calculate variance and percentage variance.
Ask AI assistance to explain any failing formula.
useCases.humanCheck: Learner ties totals back to source tables before drafting commentary.
useCases.measure: Hours from question to answered variance.
useCases.boundary: Mock figures only; analysis supports commentary, not regulatory submissions.

useCases.title: Summarising vendor spend with pivots
useCases.scenario: Vendor spend looks stable by category, but grouping by month shows a sharp change.
useCases.input: Mock purchase-order dataset with vendor, category, month and amount.
useCases.aiDoes: Pivot summaries by category and by month, with AI assistance suggesting groupings to compare.
howTo: Decide what the summary must answer.
Build a pivot by category.
Regroup by month and compare the picture.
Reconcile pivot totals to the source.
useCases.humanCheck: Learner checks the change against source rows before reporting it.
useCases.measure: Minutes to produce the summary; groupings tested.
useCases.boundary: Mock spend data only; no contract terms or commercially sensitive details in AI assistance.

useCases.title: Framing a complaint-trend question properly
useCases.scenario: Complaints appear to be rising. The answer depends on rate versus count, and which period.
useCases.input: Mock monthly complaint counts by theme with matching customer volumes, anonymised.
useCases.aiDoes: A framed question, chosen measure and tested answer; AI assistance challenges the framing.
howTo: Rewrite 'complaints are up' as a precise question.
Choose count or rate and a comparison period.
Answer it, then test another period.
Ask AI assistance for alternative interpretations to check.
useCases.humanCheck: Learner decides which measure fits; AI alternatives are tested, not adopted.
useCases.measure: Days from question to documented answer.
useCases.boundary: Aggregated mock data only; no complaint text with customer details.

useCases.title: Charting onboarding time clearly
useCases.scenario: An onboarding chart uses too many colours and axes, and nobody can say what it shows.
useCases.input: Aggregated, anonymised mock data on onboarding duration by month and stage.
useCases.aiDoes: Three simplified charts each answering one question; AI assistance suggests chart types.
howTo: Write the question each chart answers.
Ask AI assistance which chart type fits.
Build and declutter each chart in Excel.
Title each chart with its answer.
useCases.humanCheck: Learner checks each chart against the data and the question.
useCases.measure: Seconds for a peer to state each chart's answer.
useCases.boundary: Aggregated mock data only; no individual records; never used for hiring or performance decisions.

useCases.title: A dashboard a shift lead can read
useCases.scenario: A shift lead needs to see backlog and exceptions at a glance, without asking an analyst.
useCases.input: Mock servicing backlog and exception data by day and process.
useCases.aiDoes: A one-page dashboard in Excel or the dashboard tool (to be confirmed); AI assistance suggests layout.
howTo: Name the shift lead's decision.
Pick three to five measures for it.
Build the dashboard with the key measure first.
Test it with someone who has no briefing.
